newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela presses on with hydro-electric plans.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela presses on with hydro-electric plans.

text.p: Venezuela inaugurated on Thursday a major hydro-electric power station in eastern Guayana region, bringing on line an additional 2,548 megawatts (MW) to an already ambitious development along the mighty Caroni river.

The Macagua II dam at Ciudad Guayana lies 80 miles (50 km) downstream from the huge Guri power station, the second largest hydro-electric generator in the world and the jewel of state- owned Electrificacion del Caroni CA (Edelca).
Its construction marked a major step in what Edelca President Efrain Carrera called at the inauguration ceremony "an effort that began 41 years ago to harness the Caroni," an Orinoco river tributary.

Edelca now generates 73 percent of Venezuela's electric power, he said. Even with a country "blessed with abundant energy -- oil, gas, coal, everything", he promised that Edelca would press on with planned projects in Guayana in years to come.
Two projects along the Caroni, the Caruachi and Tocoma dams, are expected to be completed in 2003 and 2007, with planned installed capacities of 2,160 MW each.
Edelca is also about to sign with its Brazilian counterpart Eletrobras an agreement to extend a link across the border and sell 200 MW to the city of Boa Vista, capital of Roraima state.
Macagua, which took eleven years to build, will save Venezuela the equivalent of 76,000 barrels of oil per day, or $420 million a year at an average $15 per barrel.

President Rafael Caldera, speaking in front of up to 2,000 guests, officially gave the name "23rd of January" to the new power station, which he called a symbol of what a democratic Venezuela could do.
Venezuela celebrated on Thursday the 39th anniversary of the end of military rule when dictator Marcos Perez Jimenez was overthrown on January 23, 1958.
